children.text: The moments after a motorcycle crash can feel overwhelming. Medical bills start piling up, work may be impossible, and the insurance company often pushes for a quick payout that falls short of covering long-term needs. Knowing how to protect your rights and pursue a fair
motorcycle accident settlement
can make the difference between financial strain and real recovery. Colorado law protects injured riders, but the process requires strategy, documentation, and persistence. At
Dormer Harpring
, we help motorcyclists in Denver navigate these challenges with personal attention and a commitment to securing the resources they need to rebuild their lives.
Do You Have to Call the Police After a Motorcycle Accident?
Yes. Colorado law requires drivers to report crashes. Under

, the driver of any vehicle involved in an accident that causes injury, serious bodily injury, death, or property damage must immediately notify law enforcement and provide specified information about the incident.

This isn’t just a formality. The accident report officers often prepare becomes a key piece of evidence. It records facts such as road conditions, witness accounts, and the initial assessment of fault—details that can strongly influence an insurance company’s settlement evaluation.
Why Is It Important to Seek Medical Attention Immediately?
Many riders walk away from collisions believing their injuries are minor, only to discover days later that the damage runs deeper. Prompt medical care creates two advantages:
Health protection
: Immediate treatment ensures hidden injuries, like internal bleeding or traumatic brain injuries, are identified before complications worsen.
Legal documentation
: Medical records serve as time-stamped proof that the injuries directly resulted from the accident.

Delaying treatment allows insurers to argue that your injuries were unrelated to the collision. We recommend visiting the emergency department or an urgent care facility immediately, even when symptoms seem manageable.
Why You Should Continue Medical Treatment After a Motorcycle Accident

Stopping treatment too soon is one of the most common mistakes claimants make. Insurance carriers often comb medical records looking for “gaps in care.” If they see missed appointments or inconsistent follow-ups, they use it to minimize settlement value.
By following your physician’s treatment plan, you give yourself the best chance at recovery and strengthen your claim. Judges and juries view consistent treatment as evidence of legitimate injury.
Why Is Documenting Evidence from the Accident Crucial?

Every detail matters. Photos of the crash scene, damaged protective gear, and visible injuries provide undeniable proof of what occurred. Without this documentation, securing the full value of a motorcycle accident settlement becomes far more difficult.
What to document if you are able:
Scene photos:
Capture wide-angle shots showing traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and road conditions.
Close-ups:
Photograph motorcycle damage, skid marks, and any debris on the roadway.
Protective gear:
Helmets, gloves, boots, and jackets often show impact patterns that support your injury claims.
Witness information:
Collect names, phone numbers, and statements from bystanders who saw the crash.
Even something as simple as weather conditions or road debris can influence liability. When presented in a claim, this documentation adds layers of credibility that adjusters cannot easily dismiss.
How to Prepare Medical Bills, Lost Wages, and Damage Records for Your
Claim
A motorcycle accident settlement is only as strong as the evidence that supports it. We recommend organizing your documents into clear categories to demonstrate the full impact of your losses.
Medical bills and records:

hospital admissions, ER visits, surgeries, and follow-up appointments; rehabilitation expenses, prescriptions, and medical equipment; physician notes documenting diagnosis, treatment plans, and prognosis.
Lost income and reduced earning capacity:

Pay stubs or direct deposit records showing missed wages; employer statements confirming missed time and job restrictions; reports from vocational experts are used when injuries affect your future earning potential.
Property damage and expenses:
Estimates for motorcycle repair or replacement; receipts for helmet, clothing, or safety gear replacement damaged in the crash; appraisals for total-loss claims.

When presented in a well-documented format, these records establish the full financial toll of the crash. Our team at Dormer Harpring works closely with clients to collect, organize, and present this information so insurers cannot ignore the real value of the claim.
What You Need to Know About Motorcycle Accident Laws
Colorado follows the rule outlined in

. The law makes clear that contributory negligence does not automatically prevent recovery. An injured person may still obtain damages if their own negligence is not as great as the negligence of the party they are seeking recovery from. However, the statute requires the court (or jury) to determine the degree of negligence for each party as a percentage. Any damages awarded are then reduced in proportion to the claimant’s share of fault. If the claimant’s negligence is found to be equal to or greater than the defendant’s, the statute requires judgment in favor of the defendant.
How Long Do I Have to File a Motorcycle Accident Claim in Denver?
Colorado law sets different timeframes for filing lawsuits. Under

, tort actions for bodily injury or property damage arising out of the use or operation of a motor vehicle, such as motorcycle accidents, must generally be filed within three years of the crash. This is longer than the two-year period that applies to most other personal injury cases. Because the statute also contains exceptions and cross-references to other provisions, the best way to protect your rights is to consult a Denver motorcycle accident attorney who can calculate the correct deadline for your claim.
Tips for Maximizing Your Motorcycle Accident Settlement
There are several ways to strengthen your case:

Seek prompt follow-up care and keep all medical appointments. Consistent treatment demonstrates the seriousness of your injuries and prevents insurers from arguing that your condition is minor or unrelated to the accident.
Preserve all evidence, including protective gear. These items may show impact patterns that support your claim.
Maintain a pain journal, documenting daily limitations and emotional impact.
Consult professionals: accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and financial analysts can validate damages.
Most importantly, work with a legal team experienced in trial advocacy. Insurance companies often take settlement negotiations more seriously when they know your attorneys are prepared for court.
